declaration.preface:
This Code of Business Conduct and Ethics for the Board of Directors and Senior Management Personnel of Waaree Energies Limited (the “Company”) is adopted to ensure that the business of the Company is conducted with the highest standards of ethics and values in accordance with the applicable laws, regulations and rules and is critical to the success of the Company and to comply with the applicable rules and regulations of the SEBI (Listing Obligations & Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“Listing Regulations”).

The Board of Directors of the Company at its Meeting held on September 17, 2021 approved the Code of Conduct for the Board of Directors and Senior Management Personnel of the Company and the same shall come into force from the date of listing of the securities of the Company on recognized stock exchanges. The Board at its meeting held on 18th November 2024 further amended and approved the Code.

The Directors and the Senior Management recognize that they have fiduciary responsibility and are accountable to maximize shareholder value through good business practices and controls.

Terms not defined in the Code shall have the meaning as assigned to such terms under Companies Act, 2013, as amended and Listing Regulations.

Every employee, director and officer (“employees”) of Waaree Energies Limited (WEL) and its subsidiary companies (“WEL” or “company”), must always follow this Code when representing or working for WEL. All persons, including service providers and business partners, will be required to act consistently with our Code when acting on our behalf or in our name.
declaration.declaration:
Basic philosophy of the Code of Conduct has been guided by the practices of good corporate governance followed by the Company. The core values of the Company are:

Commitment to excellence

Integrity including honesty, openness, fairness and trust

Care for people

Dynamic and successful business organization

A Socially-valued enterprise

The Board Members and Senior Management Personnel must act within the authority conferred upon them and in the best interests of the Company and besides the duties and responsibilities cast upon Directors by applicable laws, articles of association of the Company, a Director is also expected to observe the following Code of Conduct:
declaration.scope: This policy is applicable across all WEL facilities, employees, workers, contractors, contractual workers, suppliers, and other Internal and External stakeholders globally, including the communities in which we operate. WEL extends this Ethics commitment to all relevant supply chain partners.

Integrity: Shall act honestly, diligently and in good faith in all their dealings with and for the Company.
Shall maintain confidentiality of information entrusted by the Company or acquired during the performance of their duties and shall not use it for personal gain or advantage.

Shall act in accordance with highest standards of integrity, fairness and ethical conduct while working for the Company as well as in representing the Company and also to fulfill their fiduciary obligations without their judgment being subordinated.
Conflict of Interest: Shall not involve themselves in making any decision on a subject matter in which a conflict of interest arises or could arise, between their personal interest and the interests of the Company.

In the event of apprehending such conflict of interests the relevant facts shall be disclosed in writing explaining the circumstances that would create or could create the conflicts of interests to: the Board of Directors in the case of Directors (whole-time and non-executive) & Managers and above in the case of Senior Management Personnel for further directions in the matter.
Shall not have any personal financial interests in works or contracts awarded by the Company.

Shall not have any relationship with a contractor or supplier (either directly or indirectly such as through a family member or other person or organization with which they are associated) that could compromise the ability to transact business on a professional, impartial and competitive basis or that may influence decision to be made by the Company.
Shall not hold any positions or jobs or engage in outside business or other interests that adversely affect the performance of duties of the Company.

Shall not exploit for their own personal gain, the opportunities that are discovered through Company’s business, information or position, unless the opportunity is disclosed fully in writing to the Company’s Board of Directors as the case may be.
Shall not seek to accept directly or indirectly any gifts from anyone having business dealings with the Company.
Do not make decisions that benefit you personally at the expense of WEL.
Seek approval before engaging in external employment, business ventures, or partnerships.
Do not engage in business with competitors, suppliers, or customers without disclosure and approval.
Follow formal processes for declaring conflicts of interest.
Do not use company assets or confidential information for personal gain.
Insider Trading and Confidentiality: Shall comply with all applicable laws, rules and regulations including SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading Regulations), 2015 and any violation thereon may make them personally liable.

Any information concerning the Company’s business, its customers, suppliers, etc., which is not in the public domain and to which the Board Members and Senior Management Personnel have access or possesses such information, must be considered confidential and held in confidence, unless authorized to do so and when disclosure is required under law. No Board Members and Senior Management Personnel shall provide any information either formally or informally, to the press or any other publicity media, unless specifically authorized.
Do not share confidential company information without authorization.
Do not store sensitive company data on personal devices or unauthorized cloud services.
Shareholder and Financial Integrity: The Directors shall notify the other Directors about the material personal interest in any matter and must not vote on such matter;
Shall be committed to shareholders’ worth value and shall strictly comply with all regulations and laws that govern shareholders’ right.

The shareholders shall be informed about all relevant aspects about the Company’s business and disclose such information as may be required from time to time, in accordance with applicable rules and regulations.

All books, records, accounts and financial statements will be maintained in reasonable detail, appropriately reflect transactions and conform to both applicable legal requirements and systems of internal control.

No employee including key managerial personnel or director or promoter of a listed entity shall enter into any agreement for himself /herself or on behalf of any other person, with any shareholder or any other third party with regard to compensation or profit sharing in connection with dealings in the securities of such listed entity, unless prior approval for the same has been obtained from the Board of Directors as well as public shareholders by way of an ordinary resolution.
Corruption: The Company has a zero-tolerance policy toward corruption in all its forms, including bribery, extortion, illicit payments, favours and gift. We require that all employees and partners act with integrity and avoid engaging in any activity that could be perceived as corruption. We have implemented robust internal controls to detect and prevent corrupt practices across all levels of the organization.
Do not offer, give, or accept bribes, kickbacks, gifts, or favours intended to influence business decisions.
Ensure all financial records, invoices, and payments are accurate, complete, and verifiable.
Do not manipulate, falsify, or conceal financial records.
Report any unethical financial activities, bribery attempts, or suspicious transactions to the Compliance or Internal Audit team immediately.
Refuse gifts, hospitality, or incentives from suppliers, customers, or partners that could create a conflict of interest.
Do not ignore or hide corruption risks, fraud indicators, or red flags.
Money Laundering: The Company is committed to preventing money laundering and complying with all applicable anti-money laundering (AML) regulations. We have established due diligence procedures for our ﬁnancial transactions, customer veriﬁcation processes, and regular monitoring to ensure compliance. Employees and partners are required to report any suspicious ﬁnancial activities.
Report suspicious or unusual financial transactions immediately.
Do not process transactions lacking a clear business purpose.
Verify the legitimacy and identity of all customers, vendors, and business partners (KYC/KYB).
Do not ignore red flags such as irregular payments, cash-heavy transactions, or inconsistent financial documentation.
Maintain accurate records and support documents for all financial transactions.
Do not attempt to structure payments to evade reporting obligations.
Anti-Competitive Practices: The Company ensures that it operates in a manner that promotes fair competition and complies with all applicable antitrust laws. We do not engage in anti- competitive practices such as price-ﬁxing, collusion, or bid rigging, and we ensure that our operations maintain the integrity of the competitive market.
Compete fairly and follow all antitrust and competition laws.
Do not participate in price-fixing, bid-rigging, or market allocation.
Ensure transparency in pricing, negotiations, and tender submissions.
Do not share pricing strategies or confidential data with competitors.
Promote fair business practices in supplier and customer interactions.
Do not misuse market power to exclude or harm competitors unfairly.
Fraud: The Company is committed to the prevention, detection, and mitigation of fraudulent activities at all levels. Fraud encompasses any intentional act or omission designed to deceive others, resulting in financial or reputational harm to the Company or its stakeholders. We maintain a zero-tolerance policy for fraud and have established comprehensive measures to ensure ethical and transparent business practices.
Information Security: The Company recognizes the critical importance of information security and data protection. We have comprehensive policies in place to protect sensitive and conﬁdential information from unauthorized access, use, or disclosure. Our information security management system includes regular risk assessments, employee training, and secure data handling protocols to safeguard company, employee, and customer information.
Follow WEL cybersecurity policies, including password controls and device security.
Use strong passwords, enable multi-factor authentication, and follow secure access procedures.
Report cyber threats, phishing attempts, or data breaches immediately to IT Security.
Do not click suspicious links or download unknown attachments that could compromise systems.
Sanctions and Embargoes: We are committed to complying with all applicable export and import laws, including trade sanctions, embargoes and other laws, regulations, and government orders or policies. Sanctions and embargoes restrict transactions with certain countries, named individuals and entities, and for certain end-uses. We must therefore be aware of these restrictions and obtain all documentation as may be required before engaging in a transaction or exporting our goods.
Human Rights: We are committed to respecting and protecting human rights wherever we conduct business. We prohibit the following practices and will not knowingly do business with any individual or company that participates in the following:
Exploitation of children including child labor;
Unlawful discrimination in employment and hiring practices;
Salary payments (or deductions) that illegally leave the worker below minimum wage;

targets.target: Ensure 100% of employees and contractors receive annual anti-corruption and anti-bribery training
Maintain zero conﬁrmed incidents of corruption or bribery across all operations
Conduct annual anti-corruption risk assessments across all business units and achieve 100% closure of corrective actions
Ensure 100% of high-risk functions (procurement, finance, sales, supply chain) complete enhanced ethics training each year
Ensure 100% of employees, including contractors, complete a Conflict of Interest declaration at onboarding and annually
Ensure 100% review and resolution of all COI disclosures within 30 days of reporting
Conduct annual COI awareness training for all senior management and high-risk departments
Conduct biannual fraud risk assessments across all departments
Achieve 100% completion of monthly internal fraud monitoring checks
Conduct annual third-party or statutory fraud audits across all sites
Train 100% of employees on fraud identification and reporting mechanisms
Ensure 100% of employees in finance, procurement, and commercial functions complete AML compliance training annually
Conduct annual AML audits of all financial transactions and customer/supplier due-diligence processes
Train 100% of senior management, sales, and procurement teams in competition law compliance
Conduct annual antitrust and fair-competition audits to ensure zero involvement in anti-competitive behavior
Reduce information security incidents by 20% through employee training, system upgrades, and security protocols
Conduct annually cybersecurity assessments and ensure 100% closure of identified gaps
Ensure 100% of employees complete annual information security and data privacy training
Ensure 100% compliance with internal data protection and confidentiality policies

responsibilities.duty: Provides overall oversight for the implementation of this Code, ensures adherence to SEBI LODR requirements, reviews compliance reports, and addresses any major ethical violations or governance concerns highlighted through internal or external audits.

Oversees financial integrity, anti-fraud controls, whistleblower complaints, conflict-of-interest disclosures, and ethics-related investigations. Ensures timely resolution of ethical breaches and reviews all significant compliance findings.

Leads the ethical culture of the organization, ensures accountability across all business units, reviews key risks related to ethics, AML, anti-corruption, and fraud, and ensures alignment of this policy with the company’s long-term governance strategy.

Administers the Business Conduct & Ethics framework, monitors compliance with anti-corruption, AML, anti-competitive laws, insider trading regulations, and ensures conduct of periodic ethics training and audits across all locations.

Monitors enterprise-wide fraud, corruption, data privacy, cybersecurity, and regulatory risks. Ensures preventive and corrective controls are implemented and reported through the risk governance structure as reflected in the ASR.

Ensures protection of confidential and sensitive company data, conducts quarterly cybersecurity assessments, oversees incident response systems, and ensures employee compliance with information security protocols.

Conducts periodic audits covering fraud detection, financial irregularities, conflict-of-interest checks, anti-bribery and corruption controls, AML compliance, and business conduct implementation according to ASR governance practices.

Ensures all employees sign the Code of Conduct, completes background checks, manages training on ethics, PoSH, anti-harassment, and ensures disciplinary actions for violations are implemented fairly and consistently.

Ensures compliance with applicable laws (SEBI, Companies Act, PoSH Act, AML regulations, antitrust laws, sanctions & embargo requirements). Provides legal guidance during investigations of ethical breaches.

Ensure suppliers comply with WEL’s ethical sourcing expectations, conduct due diligence, implement conflict-of-interest checks, report unethical supplier behavior, and ensure adherence to WEL’s Supplier Code of Conduct.

Promote ethical behavior within their teams, monitor day-to-day conduct, report violations promptly, ensure team participation in mandatory ethics training, and implement corrective actions when needed.

Follow the Code at all times, avoid conflicts of interest, maintain confidentiality, report unethical or suspicious activities without fear of retaliation, and support the company’s commitment to ethical and responsible conduct.

policy.monitoring:
WEL regularly conducts internal and external audits to identify any potential corruption risks. All employees are trained to recognize and report any suspicious behavior related to bribery or unethical payments.

WEL leadership reviews these disclosures and ensures they are addressed appropriately and ethically.

WEL has implemented a comprehensive fraud detection and reporting system, supported by internal audits and regular fraud awareness workshops. All employees are trained to identify fraudulent activities and report them through a conﬁdential reporting channel.

WEL implements due diligence processes, including customer veriﬁcation, transaction monitoring, and annual anti-Money laundering audits, to ensure compliance with anti-money laundering regulations.

WEl conducts regular antitrust audits to ensure compliance with anti-competitive regulations and promotes ethical business practices across all partnerships.

WEL employs a robust information security management system that includes regular cybersecurity risk assessments, secure handling of data, employee training, and encryption technologies to protect sensitive information.

Periodic audits will be conducted to ensure compliance with anti-corruption, Anti-money laundering, antitrust, and fraud prevention regulations.

All incidents of corruption, fraud, or breaches of ethical standards are promptly reported and investigated thoroughly, corrective actions are taken as appropriate and prevent future violations, promoting a culture of accountability and integrity.

The Company enforces strict disciplinary measures for violations of the Business Conduct and Ethics Policy. We ensure that all employees, contractors, and partners understand the consequences of unethical behaviour. The severity of disciplinary actions is proportional to the nature and impact of the violation.
policy.reviewMechanism:
The Code of Business Conduct and Ethics will be reviewed annually by the Board of Directors. The review will consider changes in regulations, stakeholder feedback, and company goals. Any updates will be communicated to all employees and stakeholders. Progress toward the policy's targets will also be evaluated, with adjustments made as necessary.

All members of the Board and Senior Management shall affirm compliance with this Code of conduct on an annual basis.
